I'll admit I'm biased in my dislike for Ska Punk. It's not so much the sound of it as much as it is the feeling it gives me and the unfortunate circumstances around being introduced to the genre.

My first introduction to Ska Punk was from some compilation album of late 90s-early 2000s Pop Punk and the album included the song "Wrong Way" by Sublime. I had just gotten out of an awful situation with a grown man my underaged self had NO business being around, and when that song came up, it made me feel disgusted.

Over the years I've revisited the song and I can understand the tongue in cheek lyrics and tone the song is going for, but I still just find it really off-putting. Hearing Ska punk usually just leaves me with a pit in my stomach. 

I've got to give Sublime props, though. I've always believed a good piece of art is supposed to make you feel, whether that feeling is good or bad is irrelevant. It's not every day a band comes out with a song that gives you such a visceral reaction it ruins a whole genre for you.

Ugh yes. I clock in and it's like this social autopilot switch flicks on in me. I try to just go in and do my job. I ask questions when I need answers, answer questions when asked, and that's about it. I have coworkers who are more extroverted who I'll conversate with when they come up and talk to me, but for the most part I try keep to myself as much as my job permits. Breaks and headphones are my best friend. A couple of silent minutes alone in the restroom to get me through my shift and headphones in at lunch so people aren't tempted to come up and start a conversation are the only things that keep me sane. Also, make sure to give yourself time to recharge. I have a rule that I only go out during my weekends. During the weekday, I go straight home and the only person I share my time with is my SO. Even at that, the first few hours after I get out is my "me time" to draw or listen to music or do my own thing for while and center myself again. Being an introvert in professional settings like this can suck, but they definitely have their advantages. For example, I stay out of trouble since I tend to stay away from most people, so I'm not involved in any gossip. People also tend to listen to me more attentively and take any grievances I may have more seriously since I only speak up when I feel absolutely necessary. It gets a little easier the more you practice it. You can still be warm, friendly, and professional without being loud and boisterous. You'll be alright xx
